title: The on-canvas caption field and the inspector Caption field agree
goal: While a label is being typed on the canvas, the inspector also shows a Caption field. Editing both leaves two drafts and whichever is committed last silently wins. Starting to type in one should close the other, so there is only ever one draft.
notes: CanvasNSView.beginCaptionSession / commitTextSession and EditorState.setAnnotationCaption. The simplest fix is committing the inline session when its NSTextView resigns first responder (NSTextViewDelegate.textDidEndEditing), but teardown inside that callback re-enters makeFirstResponder, so test it on the probe app rather than reasoning about it. Shipped: CanvasNSView.textDidEndEditing commits caption sessions (deferred); tool-change handler exempts caption sessions on the hand-back to Select (that was closing the fresh-arrow editor); AnnotationInspector resets its draft on editingCaptionLayerID == layer.id.
acceptance: With the on-canvas field open, clicking into the inspector Caption field closes the on-canvas field (committing its draft).
Pressing Return in the inspector never gets overwritten by a later click on the canvas.

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the fix must not touch text-tool sessions (the font picker takes focus mid-edit on purpose), must not run inside AppKit's responder hand-off (teardown re-enters makeFirstResponder), and the inspector must stay clickable while the canvas field is open (acceptance 1), so hiding it was not an option. Shortest version: commit the caption session when its text view resigns first responder, deferred a tick; reset the inspector draft when the canvas opens its own editor.

Reproduced on the probe app with a temporary in-app harness (deleted before commit) that drives the real views with synthesized events: after clicking into the inspector the inline editor stayed open, Return in the inspector landed 'inspector', and the next canvas click committed the stale canvas draft over it. Also: after the inspector Return the pill rendered behind the still-open editor.

Found a second, pre-existing defect while verifying: the caption editor that opens right after drawing an arrow closed itself one tick later. addAnnotation hands the tool back to Select, and the canvas's tool-change handler commits any open inline session. Confirmed by running the harness with the new hook disabled. Fixed in the same handler: a caption session survives the hand-back to Select; any other tool switch still commits it.

Fix: CanvasNSView.textDidEndEditing commits caption sessions (deferred a tick); the tool-change handler exempts a caption session when the new tool is Select; AnnotationInspector resets captionDraft when editingCaptionLayerID becomes this layer. Next-only in effect: every path is behind next-arrow-captions, so Current is unchanged.

Verified on the probe app: (1) canvas draft, click inspector: editor closes, draft committed, inspector shows it with caret at end; Return in inspector then canvas click keeps the inspector's text. (2) inspector draft pending, double-click arrow: editor opens with the real caption, inspector drops its draft, then follows the canvas commit. (3) inspector draft pending, draw a new arrow: editor opens on the new arrow, inspector empty. (4) draw, type, click inspector: label kept; switching to another tool with the editor open commits the draft.

Scripts/test.sh: 1187 tests green on the third run. Runs one and two each failed a different timing-budget test in the ElementBounds hover suite by under a millisecond (56 ms vs 50, 30.6 ms vs 30) while the machine was busy; unrelated to this change (PhotonzCore, no app code), follow-up filed.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-02-arrow-caption-one-draft.json. Not done: inspector Caption field still commits only on Return (raised as a question in the audit rather than changed).

Caption fields share one draft: the canvas editor commits when it loses focus (click into the inspector), the inspector drops its draft when the canvas opens its editor, and the fresh-arrow editor no longer closes itself on the hand-back to Select. Sources/Photonz/CanvasView.swift and LayersPanel.swift, Next flag only. Verified on the probe app with synthesized events (four scenarios) and Scripts/test.sh green (1187). Audit queue/audits/2026-09-02-arrow-caption-one-draft.json.
